note: After the original description of the new species by Light (1930) (in English); the soldier and the large nymph have full prose descriptions and measurement tables, the alate being recorded in the original as 'Adult. Unknown.' and not described. The original also gives diagnoses for the soldier and the nymph. Several entries of the small-individual column of the measurement table are OCR-damaged, so only the legible values are recorded here.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head dorsally passing from yellow-brown behind to red-brown in front, ventrally pale yellowish brown, darker anteriorly. Body pale translucent brown over a milky white ground, dirty grey patches visible through the posterior wall. Legs white. Head, body and legs with many brown hairs of various sizes, a considerable number of them long setae. Head thick, broad, rectangular, flattened above and below; posterolateral corners broadly rounded, the sides rounded and passing into the flat upper and lower surfaces. Cranial sutures distinct; frons steeply sloping, with a broad shallow depression in the middle. Eyes not projecting above the surface, longitudinally oval, transparent externally and milky white internally. Postclypeus indistinctly delimited; anteclypeus very short and white. Labrum very small, width clearly greater than length, the short sides rounded into a broadly convex anterior margin. Upper margin of the antennal socket slightly projecting, but far less so than in other species of the genus. Mandibles short and stout, less than half the head length; base inflated and irregular, dark red-brown to red-black, the distal part dark red-black to black; distal half upturned, not strongly incurved; left mandible only slightly incurved at the tip; right mandible shorter than the left, thicker distally and more strongly incurved, the curved part occupying more than half its length; the posterior half, which bears no teeth, rough on its inner face. Antennae 15-segmented, segment 1 largest, segment 4 smallest, segment 3 second to segment 1, heavily sclerotized and, apart from segment 1, the widest; segment 2 larger than segments 4 and 5 and equal to segment 6. Pronotum narrow longitudinally and broad transversely, wider than the head when spread out, length clearly less than half its own width; anterior margin very shallowly concave, the anterior half of the sides convex and the posterior half converging, posterior margin almost straight; posterior margins of mesonotum and metanotum shallowly concave. Thorax and abdomen broad and flat; cerci small, styli long and slender.

sections.label: Nymph
sections.text: Large nymph: head and thorax milky white to pale yellow; abdomen dirty grey, from the gut contents; head and body with a moderate number of yellowish brown hairs contrasting with the milky white body, especially on the head and thorax; a distinct dark spot at the inner mandibular articulation; mandibles pale yellow, becoming dark red-brown towards the tip. Large nymph: head thick, subcircular in dorsal view; antennae more than 15-segmented, segments 1 and 2 cylindrical, segment 3 inverted-conical (often showing incomplete division), segments 4 to 6 or 7 more or less disc-like; segment 1 largest, segment 3 as long as segment 2, segment 4 very short, segments 5 to 11 gradually larger, the terminal segment narrow and oval. Eyes small, unpigmented, composed of a few ommatidia, hardly visible except by dissection. Pronotum with the anterior margin distinctly concave and the posterior margin convex, the sides converging posteriorly; overall appearing folded forwards from the midline to each side.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Soldier measurements (mm, minimum—maximum): body length 9.0—11.0; head length with mandibles 4.95 (this row is OCR-damaged for the small individual, only the large-individual value survives); head length without mandibles (to the outer mandibular articulation) 2.88—3.15; head width 2.34—2.61; pronotum length in situ 1.10—1.17, spread width 2.52 (in-situ width OCR-damaged); pronotum length in situ 1.02 (this row is a separate row of the original book). Large nymph measurements (mm): body length 9.5; head length 2.07; head length to frontoclypeal suture 1.44; head width 2.00; pronotum width 1.93 before and 2.16 after dissection; pronotum length 1.00. Type locality Mount Maquiling, Laguna Province, Luzon, collection number 965, collected by E. H. Taylor in 1922, month 12 (December), at 700 m elevation, 'in galleries in the heartwood of living trees'. The alate is recorded in the original as Unknown.
